clue.text: Large bottle in vehicle next to young man

blocks.note: a car is a vehicle
a boy is a young male

explanation.surface: A big bottle is sitting in a car beside a youth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' looks like it puts the bottle inside the vehicle, but it only links the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A carboy is a big glass or plastic container, often cushioned in a crate, used for liquids such as acids.

clue.text: A duke to prepare a speech

blocks.note: taken as written
D is the abbreviation for duke
to dress food or a wound is to prepare it

explanation.surface: A nobleman sets about drafting a talk.
explanation.definitionFit: An address is a formal talk delivered to an audience, so it is a speech.

clue.text: Angry voice demanding fish

blocks.note: as in a black look or a black mood
a bass is the lowest singing voice

explanation.surface: Someone shouts furiously, insisting on having fish.
explanation.definitionFit: The black bass is a North American freshwater game species, so it is a kind of fish.

clue.text: Ferment in still, for instance, within

indicators.note: within means inside, so one piece is placed in the middle of the other

blocks.note: yet means still, as in not yet done
as can mean for instance, as in big cats, as lions

explanation.surface: Fermentation happening inside a still, say.
explanation.walkthrough: 'still' looks like distilling equipment, which suits the brewing picture, but it is the adverb.
explanation.definitionFit: Yeast is the fungus that causes fermentation, and the word ferment can also mean such an agent.

clue.text: Conflict involving eastern river

indicators.note: to involve something is to take it in, so one piece wraps round the other

blocks.note: a war is a conflict
E is the abbreviation for eastern

explanation.surface: A war breaks out in the east, along some river.
explanation.walkthrough: The Wear is a river in north-east England, flowing through Durham and Sunderland.
explanation.definitionFit: The Wear is a named English watercourse, so it is an example of a river.

clue.text: Bet a bundle about US actor

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece goes round the other

blocks.note: a wad is a bundle, especially of banknotes
Richard Gere, the American film star

explanation.surface: Someone put a pile of money on a Hollywood star.
explanation.definitionFit: Wagered is the past tense of wager, so it means placed a bet, matching bet used as a past tense.

clue.text: Capone left early, or soon enough

blocks.note: Al Capone, the Chicago gangster
L is the abbreviation for left
to be in good time is to be early

explanation.surface: The gangster departed ahead of schedule, or at least promptly.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means eventually, at the proper moment, so it says something will happen soon enough.

clue.text: Fruit, extremely unattractive by the sound of it

indicators.note: this phrase tells us to judge the word by how it is pronounced, not how it is written

blocks.note: being extremely unattractive means being plain-looking in the worst way

explanation.surface: A fruit that seems, from its name, to be really ugly.
explanation.walkthrough: The ugli fruit is a lumpy Jamaican citrus hybrid whose trade name is a play on its looks.
explanation.definitionFit: The ugli is a citrus cross of grapefruit and tangerine, so it is a fruit.

clue.text: Vigilante revealed in newspaper article member brought back

indicators.note: bringing something back sends it the way it came, so the word is read from end to start

blocks.note: the Guardian is a British national newspaper
an indefinite article
a leg is a limb, i.e. a member of the body

explanation.surface: A newspaper article exposes a vigilante who turns out to be a member of some group.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pulls 'newspaper article' together as one thing; it is two pieces, the paper's name and the little word 'an'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Guardian Angels are a volunteer street-patrol organisation, so one of their members is a self-appointed vigilante.

clue.text: Where lots may go to join in a game

blocks.note: items for sale are called lots at a sale-room
to bridge two things is to join them

explanation.surface: A puzzling description of a place many people head to in order to sign up for a game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lots' looks like many people, but it means items up for sale.
explanation.definitionFit: Auction bridge is an older form of the card game in which players bid for the contract.

clue.text: Tricky question from trustee about wealth

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one piece is wrapped round the other

blocks.note: Tr. is a dictionary abbreviation for trustee
ease in the sense of affluence, freedom from want, as in a life of ease

explanation.surface: A hard question posed by someone managing a fortune.
explanation.definitionFit: A teaser, short for brain-teaser, is a puzzling problem, so it is a tricky question.

clue.text: Under control, one north European on the radio

indicators.note: on the radio we only hear words, so the spelling can differ from a word with the same sound

blocks.note: the Roman numeral for one
N is the abbreviation for north
a Czech is a European, and the word is pronounced like a restraint

explanation.surface: A broadcast about keeping things under control, featuring a European from the north.
explanation.definitionFit: To hold something in check is to restrain it, keeping it under control.

clue.text: Dramatist in centre, high on Ecstasy

indicators.note: someone high on drugs is not in their right state, so these letters are jumbled up

blocks.note: taken as written
E is slang for the drug Ecstasy

explanation.surface: A playwright in the middle of things, high on drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' simply adds the drug's letter to the word in front.
explanation.definitionFit: Terence was a Roman comic playwright of the second century BC, so he is a dramatist.

clue.text: A girl, out of order

blocks.note: taken as written
a miss is a girl or young woman

explanation.surface: A young woman is told off for behaving badly.
explanation.definitionFit: If something is amiss it is wrong or faulty, which is what out of order means.

clue.text: Comfortable, ready to receive visitors

blocks.note: first meaning: at ease, relaxed
second meaning: in one's own house and willing to see callers

explanation.surface: A relaxed host prepared for guests to arrive.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both feeling at ease and being in one's house to receive callers.

clue.text: Hard-working animal given to one couple, American

blocks.note: an ass is a donkey
the Roman numeral for one
a duo is a pair
US is short for American, as in the US

explanation.surface: A hard-working donkey is handed over to one American couple.
explanation.definitionFit: Assiduous means diligent and persevering, showing constant careful effort.

clue.text: Rascal's expression of surprise

blocks.note: first meaning: a rogue, often said affectionately
second meaning: an exclamation of astonishment

explanation.surface: A scoundrel's exclamation when startled.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is both a jocular term for a scamp and an exclamation of amazement.

clue.text: Groupies annoy lad after end of sesh

definitions.note: plural noun; the answer is the plural of hanger-on

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, so only that one is kept

blocks.note: the last letter of sesh, slang for a drinking session
to anger is to annoy
a son is a boy, a lad

explanation.surface: Fans irritate a young man once a drinking session finishes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' tells us the first two pieces follow the letter from sesh.
explanation.definitionFit: Groupies are fans who attach themselves to celebrities, which is what hangers-on do.

clue.text: Type of punt travelling in either direction?

blocks.note: first meaning: a punt is a bet, and this kind of bet pays if the horse wins or is placed
second meaning, whimsical: going both ways

explanation.surface: A flat-bottomed boat that can go forwards or backwards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'punt' suggests a boat on the river, but it is British slang for a bet; the question mark flags the playful second reading.
explanation.definitionFit: In horse-race betting an each-way bet backs a horse both to win and to be placed.

clue.text: The lowest point, notice, in Northern Ireland

indicators.note: one thing being in another means it sits inside it

blocks.note: NIR is the official code for Northern Ireland
an ad is an advertisement, a notice

explanation.surface: A public notice in Northern Ireland marks the lowest ebb.
explanation.walkthrough: Northern Ireland's usual abbreviation is NI, but its official code, as in GB-NIR, has three letters; the notice goes after the first.
explanation.definitionFit: The nadir is the point directly below the observer, and by extension the worst or lowest moment.

clue.text: Kipper? See awfully keen chef initially holding it up?

indicators.note: awfully suggests something done badly, so these letters come out in a mangled order
initially points at the start of a word, so just its opening letter is used
holding means gripping inside, so the jumbled letters wrap around another piece
in a down clue, up means the word is written from the bottom upwards

blocks.note: taken as written
the opening letter of chef
taken as written

explanation.surface: A smoked fish is on offer; look how an eager cook is holding it aloft.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kipper' looks like the smoked herring, which suits the chef, but a kipper tie is a very wide necktie fashionable in the 1960s and 70s.
explanation.definitionFit: A kipper is a broad, brightly patterned tie, so it is a type of necktie.

clue.text: I'm clear, racing in amazing event

indicators.note: racing suggests rushing about wildly, so these letters are thrown into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A competitor says they are out in front while racing, an astonishing turn of events.
explanation.definitionFit: A miracle is an extraordinary, wonderful occurrence, which is an amazing event.

clue.text: Live way out round foot of dales

indicators.note: round means encircling, so one piece goes around the other
in a down clue the foot of a word is its bottom, its last letter

blocks.note: an exit is a way out
the final letter of dales

explanation.surface: Living a remote life somewhere around the bottom of the Yorkshire Dales.
explanation.walkthrough: 'foot of dales' sounds like a place at the base of the valleys.
explanation.definitionFit: To exist is to be alive, so the verb is a synonym for live.

clue.text: Rebellious group in key legal case

blocks.note: F is a musical key
an action is a lawsuit

explanation.surface: A band of dissidents caught up in an important court case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'key' reads as an adjective meaning important, but it is a musical key.
explanation.definitionFit: A faction is a dissenting group within a larger body, often in rebellion against it.

clue.text: Bill's memo

blocks.note: first meaning: a banknote
second meaning: a short written message

explanation.surface: A man named Bill has written a memo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bill' looks like a man's name; it is paper money.
explanation.definitionFit: A note is both a piece of paper currency and a brief jotted reminder.

clue.text: The PM's way?

blocks.note: surface reading: the Prime Minister's method or manner of doing things
setter's reading: a way is also a road, and the British Prime Minister lives on a famous London road

explanation.walkthrough: 'way' looks like a manner or style but is a street; the PM's official residence is Number 10 on this road.
explanation.definitionFit: The street in Westminster holding the Prime Minister's residence is literally the PM's road.

clue.text: Frightfully clever yuppie? To some extent

indicators.note: to some extent means only partly, so the letters are a portion of the words before

blocks.note: found spanning the end of the first word and start of the second

explanation.surface: Is a smart young professional really that clever? Only partly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Frightfully' reads as describing the cleverness, but it is the definition, in its intensifying sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Frightfully is used as an intensifier, as in frightfully good, meaning extremely.

clue.text: Sensitive proposal

blocks.note: first meaning: sore or painful to touch
second meaning: a formal offer, as in a bid for a contract

explanation.surface: A delicate suggestion, perhaps one of marriage.
explanation.definitionFit: The word works as an adjective for being sore to touch and as a noun for a formal bid or offer.
